results.name: familiar_outlier_excuse_contrast
results.description: In >=3-example sets where all but one example share a final digit or a parity, yes rate for non-example targets obeying that majority rule when the lone outlier is a familiar number (1, 100, power of 2, square, 27, multiple of 10) minus when it is unremarkable; observed below null means people do not excuse familiar outliers more than plain ones as much as the familiar-stray model predicts, above means they excuse them even more.

results.name: clean_rule_member_inside_minus_outside_hull
results.description: In >=2-example sets whose examples all belong to some rule of <=25 members, yes rate for non-example members of the smallest such rule lying inside the examples' range minus those lying outside it; observed above null means people restrict a rule to the examples' magnitude range more than the model (which adds range only via its separate interval hypotheses), below means less.

results.name: clean_small_rule_member_yes
results.description: In >=3-example sets whose examples all belong to some rule of <=25 members, yes rate for non-example members of the smallest such rule; observed above null means people trust a clean rule more (endorse its members more) than the model's uncertain-reliability/interval mixture predicts, below means less.

results.name: clean_rule_inhull_nonmember_yes
results.description: In >=2-example sets whose examples all belong to some rule of <=25 members, yes rate for targets strictly inside the examples' range that belong to no rule containing all examples; observed above null means people let magnitude similarity override a clean rule more than the model's interval component predicts, below means they reject such in-range non-members more strictly.

results.name: unsupported_familiar_target_bias
results.description: Among non-example targets not supported by the examples (every non-parity, non-contains-digit rule containing the target holds fewer than half the examples), yes rate for familiar targets (1, 100, squares, cubes, powers of 2, multiples of 10) minus other targets; observed above null means people endorse familiar numbers regardless of the examples (a target-familiarity bias the model lacks), below means they avoid them.

results.name: single_example_tiny_rule_partner_yes
results.description: In single-example sets, yes rate for targets sharing with the example a rule of <=7 members (e.g. 25->5, 3->81, 10->100), minus yes rate for other targets; observed below null means people use tiny rules (powers of m, cubes) less than the equal rule prior plus size principle predicts, above means more.

results.name: outlier_neighbourhood_generalisation
results.description: In >=3-example sets where a rule of <=25 members (not parity/contains-digit) holds all but one example, yes rate for targets outside that rule within 5 of the outlier minus yes rate for targets outside the rule more than 10 from every example; observed above null means people generalise from the stray example's neighbourhood (treat it as informative) more than the model, which explains it as noise, below means less.

results.name: full_cover_broad_vs_partial_narrow_contrast
results.description: In >=3-example sets where a smaller rule holds exactly all-but-one example and a larger rule (<=34 members) holds every example, yes rate for non-example targets in the larger rule only minus targets in the smaller rule only; observed above null means people prefer the rule explaining every example over the tighter rule-plus-stray more than the model's reliability belief predicts, below means they accept a stray to keep the tighter rule more readily.
